summary: Plan a Mae Rim day around Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden’s glasshouses, mountain grounds and canopy walkway, with a separately booked flower farm or café if current seasonal blooms appeal. It is a scenic garden outing, not a single December festival; flower-farm seasons and blooms vary.
whyGo: Explore a large mountain botanic garden with collections, rainforest glasshouse and treetop walkway.
Pair the garden with a seasonal flower farm and café for a relaxed day outside Chiang Mai.
bestFor: Plant lovers, families and photographers who enjoy an unhurried outdoor day.
Travellers with private transport who want to combine several Mae Rim stops.
skipIf: You need a guaranteed flower display: specific fields and bloom dates change by season.
You want a compact, walkable attraction close to central Chiang Mai.
duration: Allow 5–7 hours including city transfers and one or two stops; this is a planning estimate. The botanic garden alone merits at least 2–3 hours.
cost: TAT currently lists Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden admission at THB 50 for adults and free for children under 12. A government tourism directory has conflicting rates and lists internal vehicle fees; confirm the complete current tariff directly before travel. TAT’s I Love Flower Farm listing gives THB 70 including tea and a snack, but seasonal operation and 2026 rates need confirmation. Transport and café purchases are extra.
hours: TAT lists Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden daily 08:30–17:00. The tourism directory lists 08:30–16:30, so verify closing time and last entry with the garden. TAT lists I Love Flower Farm daily 08:00–18:00, subject to seasonal operation and advance reservation.
bestTime: Start in the morning for cooler walking and leave time for the garden’s hilly grounds. Weekdays are a reasonable crowd-avoidance choice; holiday traffic can add delays.
gettingThere: Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden is in Mae Rim, about 27 km from Chiang Mai according to the government tourism directory. Arrange a private driver or rental car for the day; garden and flower-farm stops are spread out and public transport details are not confirmed. Ask the driver to wait or agree a pickup time before entering each venue.
booking: The botanic garden is a walk-in visit according to the available visitor listings, but confirm current entry arrangements and any internal transport. TAT says I Love Flower Farm requires advance booking and limits daily visitors; contact it directly and confirm that it is open for your date before building the itinerary around it.
accessibility: The garden covers extensive, hilly grounds, and the canopy walkway includes elevated walking; step-free access across the full site is not verified. Ask the garden about accessible drop-off, internal transport, toilets and current walkway access. Flower fields may have uneven ground.
practicalTips: Check garden opening hours, entry fees and internal vehicle charges with Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden before departure; published government listings differ.
Confirm flower-farm opening, bloom conditions, reservation and return transport directly; older seasonal articles do not establish December 2026 availability.
Wear comfortable shoes and bring water, sun protection and a light layer for the hills.
decemberNotes: Cool-season flowers are a draw in Mae Rim, but no source reviewed confirms particular flower-farm dates or a December 2026 event schedule. A previous Botanic Festival ran 24 December 2025–4 January 2026; do not assume it will repeat on those dates. Expect higher demand around Christmas and New Year and confirm any farm booking well ahead.
uncertainties: Published entry details conflict: TAT currently lists adult admission at THB 50 and daily hours to 17:00, while a government tourism directory shows different rates and 16:30 closing. Confirm with the garden.
No confirmed December 2026 flower-farm bloom calendar or Botanic Festival dates were found.
Current accessibility details, internal garden transport charges and public transport options need direct confirmation.
